newsitem.title: USA: Republican dissaray might thwart tax deal - Raines.
newsitem.headline: Republican dissaray might thwart tax deal - Raines.

text.p: White House budget director Franklin Raines raised concern Sunday that disarray in the Republican leadership could undermine talks between the Clinton administration and Congress on a tax cut bill.

Following an apparent attempt last week by party rebels to oust House Speaker Newt Gingrich, Raines said Republican leaders might try to appease conservatives by moving away from a compromise with President Clinton on tax cut priorities.

"And our concern would be that in the effort to deal with the internal politics, that it would cause a lurch from the mainstream that would make it impossible to put together a mainstream budget and tax bill," he said on ABC television's "This Week" show.

House and Senate tax negotiators are trying to hash out a tax cut bill that Clinton would be willing to sign, to carry out a May budget agreement between congressional leaders and the White House that called for $85 billion in net tax cuts over five years.

In a letter to the negotiators Saturday, Clinton said tax relief in the House and Senate tax bills was weighted too heavily toward the wealthy, while the Republicans insisted that their bills would largely benefit the middle class.
Several Republicans Sunday said they wanted to put the leadership strife behind them at least until the budget deal was carried out.

"I support the speaker, and the speaker's going to continue to be our leader. And we're progressing now with these budget negotiations in a very, very constructive way. And this is not interfering with it," Representative Bill Archer, chairman of the House Ways and Means Committee, said on "This Week".
"The president wants to sign a bill, and we want a bill signed," the Texas Republican said. "And I'm satisfied they're going to get it and that we'll come together on this."
